primary_claim: Standard L1-trained crosscoders hallucinate most of their apparent 'chat-only' latents due to shrinkage and latent-decoupling artifacts; switching to BatchTopK crosscoders and, further, diff-SAEs trained on chat-base activation differences recover far more of the true behavioral difference between base and chat models (88% of the KL gap for diff-SAEs vs 60% for crosscoders).
contradicts_or_qualifies: Questions whether crosscoders (Anthropic's proposed default sparse dictionary technique for model diffing) should remain the default, given their inherent bias toward shared latents and hallucinated chat-only latents
stated_future_work: Developing an evaluation framework using model organisms with known modifications (e.g. synthetic document finetuning) to measure whether diffing methods find what they're supposed to find
Using model diffing to debug specific model behaviors, e.g. backtracking in reasoning models
Weight-based analysis: decomposing weight differences directly instead of activations, e.g. via LoRA adapters or parameter decomposition
Scaling harmful behaviors: using model diffing to amplify low-probability harmful behaviors introduced by fine-tuning to make them detectable
limitations_stated: Without knowing what the 'right answer' looks like, it's hard to compare diffing methods objectively

Applying latent scaling to a base-model SAE did not yield interpretable 'chat-specific' latents, for reasons including template-token interference, lack of causality filtering, or insufficient base SAE capacity
Crosscoders have an inherent architectural bias toward learning shared latents, which can miss subtler model-specific differences
quote: Crosscoders leave significant behavioral differences on the table: when we use the crosscoder's full reconstruction of the difference, we only recover 60% of the KL gap.
